name: Banana
lede: Banana is a pale lemon yellow named for the fruit, and the books we hold say very little about it.

sections.title: A fruit name
sections.body:
Banana belongs to a large class of color names taken from fruit. Garfield counts 254 fruit names in a catalog of color names, with apricot and banana as examples [1]. Paterson lists banana among its yellows, and records the slang "mellow yellow" for a banana skin smoked as an intoxicant [2]. The swatch is a bright pale yellow, near [[canary]] and [[lemon-yellow]], and paler than [[butterscotch]].

Who first used the name for a color is undocumented in our sources. It sits in the [[yellow]] family.

sections.title: Seeing it
sections.body: Eckstut and Siegel use a blue banana to make a point about value: a picture can use an "inaccurate" hue and still read correctly if the lightness is right [3]. That is a useful reminder that a picture of a banana can lean on lightness as much as on hue, and that this pale tone sits at the light end of the yellows beside [[canary]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Banana is almost absent from our paintings. Only one painting in 23,781 holds it, as photographed [4]. A pale screen yellow like this is rare in aged, varnished oils, where varnish pushes yellows darker, so the figure says more about varnish than about painters [4].

origin.named_after: the fruit; first use as a color undocumented
